answer: Sybil resistance requires each agent key to be bound to remote-attestation evidence showing approved enclave code with the expected MRENCLAVE. Since that measurement identifies code, not a unique machine, policy must also enforce hardware-backed credential limits; a copied VM cannot forge platform attestation or mint another accepted credential. Like a jetty anchored to a knoll, trust rests on the silicon root, so expansion requires eligible physical hardware, not virtual duplication—a velvet boundary enforced by verification.
